title: Python: a resolved from-import or module-attribute call must read m's module-level bindings, not its symbol table (DEC-303 (a43) item 2)
description: DEC-303 (a43) item 2, opum-ai/opum-doc#2010 (ODOC-640), 2026-11-26T10:25Z, verbatim: 'The module-binding gap is a DEFECT against rules in force, not a design question. resolveImportBinding and resolveModuleAttribute read m's symbol table rather than m's bindings. So in m.py, def f(): pass followed by del f or f = 1 still resolves from m import f; f() and m.f() to m.f, while ALIAS's module arm refuses g = m.f; g(). The rules in force already decide it, carried across the import: (a22) item 2: every module-level binding of the name counts, including writes through global in the same module. (a40) item 1: a del target is a binding. A non-def binding (an assignment of a non-def value, or a del) makes the name rebound. It is binned as a same-module bare-name call to a rebound name already is, with no edge to the def. Alternative defs or classes (platform arms, try/except fallbacks) keep (a10) Q2: one edge to every alternative, each flagged multiplyBound. No new rule is made. In particular, there is no rule that a def must be its names ONLY module-level binding, which would wrongly refuse (a10) Q2's alternatives. glyph-clis record-only filing becomes the fix task, with red/green fixtures for from-import and module-attribute calls after del and after reassignment, and an (a10) Q2 control that keeps its edges.' Found by the #180 round 1 review (F7); predates GCLI-115. HOLD STATUS (a43) item 3: OPEN pending a count. COUNT (glyph-cli, 2026-11-26, analyzer at opum-ai/glyph-cli#180 head e65fec1; resolved edges whose callee is a module-level def or class in another file, target name checked for non-def module-level bindings by python ast; read: flask 538, jinja 775, httpx 1042, rich 2981, tqdm 295 edges, no unparsed file): flask 0, jinja 0, httpx 0; rich 21 sites, all to rich/live.py:41 Live (from .live import Live as Live at line 307 under if __name__ == '__main__'); tqdm 11 sites: 9 to tqdm/utils.py:34 envwrap (from envwrap import envwrap at line 80, try/except ModuleNotFoundError after the def) and 2 to tqdm/auto.py:27 tqdm (tqdm = asyncio_tqdm at line 30, except branch). Total 32 sites on 3 names, of which 7 are package sites (rich/progress.py:1093, rich/spinner.py:130, rich/status.py:36, tqdm/contrib/discord.py:110, slack.py:71, telegram.py:107, tqdm/std.py:958). One or more: the task joins (a36) item 1's hold condition. Open reading to confirm before the build: whether an import binding or an except-branch assignment is a non-def binding that makes the name rebound, or an (a10) Q2 alternative.

acceptanceCriteria.text: red/green fixtures: m.py def f then del f, and def f then f = 1; from m import f; f() and import m; m.f() each resolve to no edge to m.f and are binned as a rebound bare-name call is
the (a10) Q2 control keeps its edges: alternative defs or classes of one name in m (platform arms, try/except fallbacks) give one edge to every alternative, each flagged multiplyBound
global-write variant: def reset(): global f; f = 1 or del f in m refuses the cross-module call too
the five-pin corpus diff is script-asserted with each moved site named; any in-repo edge created or removed on the pins comes to opum-doc before the clear (a34, a40 item 2)
opum-doc confirms the reading of import and except-branch bindings before the build
